messages.subject: WLS.V
parts:
Hello community,

I tried to fit a cfa via getCov. I therefore used a polychoric, polyserial correlation matrix as input. I failed to use DWLS or the ordered=v(") function by fitting the cfa. There was a warning while using DWLS saying that: 'lavaan ERROR: the (D)WLS estimator is only available with full data or with a user-provided WLS.V'

Can someone please describe how to merge a user-provided WLS.V and how to implement it while fitting a cfa with polychoric, polyserial correlation matrix and ordered=v(") function. An example of how to put it together would be great.

Thank you very much!

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: WLS.V
parts:
On 12/05/2015 03:36 AM, Tino wrote:
> I tried to fit a cfa via getCov. I therefore used a polychoric,
> polyserial correlation matrix as input. I failed to use DWLS or the
> ordered=v(") function by fitting the cfa. There was a warning while
> using DWLS saying that: 'lavaan ERROR: the (D)WLS estimator is only
> available with full data or with a user-provided WLS.V'

Indeed. Without full data, you can not compute WLS.V. If the correlation
matrix came to you as 'given', and you have no access to the original
data that was used to create it, you can not use lavaan using WLS and
friends. At best, you can treat the data as continuous, use ML, and get
suboptimal results.
> Can someone please describe how to merge a user-provided WLS.V

That is not an easy task. And it requires full data. The canonical
reference is Muthen 1984.

There are various ways to compute this WLS.V matrix, and that is the
reason why we have this WLS.V argument: to study the effect of different
WLS.V flavors on the quality of the estimates/inference.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: WLS.V
parts:
First thing you should know is that WLS.V is the (inverse) of the
asymptotic variance matrix of the *sample statistics*. It has nothing
to do with 'observation weights'. Think of it as 'sample statistics
weights'.

So if you have, say 5 binary observed variables (and no x-covariates),
the sample statistics are: 5*(5-1)/2 = 10 correlations, and 5
thresholds. The dimension of WLS.V will be 15 x 15.

Small example:

# create binary version of Holzinger & Swineford data
HS9 <- HolzingerSwineford1939[,c("x1","x2","x3","x4","x5",
"x6","x7","x8","x9")]
HSbinary <- as.data.frame( lapply(HS9, cut, 2, labels=FALSE) )

# 5 binary observed variables
model <- ' trait =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 '

# use estimator "WLS" to show the full weight matrix
fit <- cfa(model, data=HSbinary, ordered=names(HSbinary), std.lv=TRUE,
estimator = "WLS")
inspect(fit, "WLS.V")

In lavaan (0.5-20), the first 5 rows/cols correspond with the
thresholds, the last 10 rows/cols correspond with the correlations. When
estimator = "DWLS" (the default), only the diagonal of this weight
matrix is used.

Yves.
